work.title: The Life of Timon of Athens

scene.label: Act 3, Scene 4
scene.title: SCENE IV. A hall in Timon's house

content.text: Enter two of Varro's Servants meeting Titus and Hortensius and then Lucius, all Servants of Timon's creditors, to wait for his coming out.

lines.text: Well met, good morrow, Titus and Hortensius.
lines.plainText: Well met good morrow Titus and Hortensius

lines.text: The like to you, kind Varro.
lines.plainText: The like to you kind Varro

lines.text: Lucius!
lines.plainText: Lucius

lines.plainText: What do we meet together

lines.text: Ay, and I think

lines.plainText: One business does command us all

lines.text: For mine is money.
lines.plainText: For mine is money

lines.text: So is theirs and ours.

lines.plainText: That is one may reach deep enough and yet

lines.plainText: I am of your fear for that

lines.text: Yes, mine's three thousand crowns. What's yours?

content.text: Enter Flavius in a cloak, muffled.

lines.plainText: I have no more to reckon he to spend

lines.plainText: Ay but this answer will not serve

lines.text: If 'twill not serve, 'tis not so base as you,
lines.plainText: If 'twill not serve 'tis not so base as you

lines.text: For you serve knaves.
lines.plainText: For you serve knaves

lines.text: No matter what, he's poor, and that's revenge enough. Who can speak broader than he that has no house to put his head in? Such may rail against great buildings.

lines.text: O, here's Servilius; now we shall know some answer.
lines.plainText: O here's Servilius now we shall know some answer

lines.text: If I might beseech you, gentlemen, to repair some other hour, I should derive much from't. For take't of my soul, my lord leans wondrously to discontent. His comfortable temper has forsook him, he's much out of health and keeps his chamber.

lines.text: Good gods!

lines.plainText: The place which I have feasted does it now

lines.plainText: Put in now Titus

lines.plainText: Here's mine

lines.plainText: Cut my heart in sums
